summary: Iter99 retest of iter98 HIGH-priority RBAC finding on /api/customers/*. 20/20 tests passed. The salesman→customer scoping fix in /app/backend/routes/customers.py (_salesman_customer_filter helper + chained {customer_name: {$in: [...]}} filter on outstanding, followups, targets, payment-behavior, ledger/export) is working correctly. Admin/super_admin tenant view unchanged. Iter98 agent-endpoint hardening, tenant isolation and auth regression all still green.
critical_code_review_comments: _salesman_customer_filter() in routes/customers.py:46 — clean implementation. Tries exact match first, falls back to case-insensitive regex. Returns [] for unmapped salesman (locks them out, correct) and None for non-salesman roles (no extra filter, correct).

Live numbers confirm the fix: admin sees 37 / 0 / 39 / 37 (full) on outstanding/followups/targets/payment-behavior, salesman ravi sees 1 / 0 / 0 / 1 (only 'Ankit Automobiles, Indore'). Previously was 83 customers leaking.
Ledger export now correctly rejects 'Krishna Sales Corporation' for ravi with 'Access denied for this customer', and allows 'Ankit Automobiles, Indore'.
All iter98 sync_token enforcement tests (sync, reconcile, commands GET hard-reject; sync-progress and commands/ack soft-allow) still pass. /agent/latest-version + /check-update still green.
Tenant isolation across X-Company-ID header forgery still intact — demo cannot read admin tenant.

Note: the fix uses customer NAME-based filtering ({customer_name: {$in: [...]}}). Names are unique-per-tenant in this schema and the salesman_master.fy_customers maps salesman→list-of-names per FY, so this is consistent. If at some future point names become non-unique, switch to customer_id mapping.

Edge case verified: a salesman with NO salesman_master row (or no mapping for current FY) gets an empty payload, not the full tenant. Helper returns [] in that case and the route short-circuits to {customers:[], total_outstanding:0, total_paid:0}.

rca_of_the_issue: PREVIOUS ROOT CAUSE (iter98): _build_query in routes/customers.py only filtered tenant_id/company_id, never inspected ctx.user.role. APPLIED FIX: New _salesman_customer_filter(ctx) helper looks up salesman_master.fy_customers[current_fy] for the logged-in salesman's name and returns the list of mapped customer names. Each /customers/* endpoint calls this helper after _build_query and, when the role is salesman, chains {customer_name: {$in: mapped_list}} into the Mongo query. ledger/export checks the requested customer_name against the same list and returns 'Access denied for this customer' on mismatch. VERIFIED: admin still sees full 37-row tenant, salesman ravi sees 1 row (only Ankit Automobiles, Indore). All 20 regression assertions pass.
